argument_summary: The present admissible record supports only a narrow defense of certification. It shows overall launch readiness passed by 2.2 percentage points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and public governance guidance supports certification with documented limitations and post-launch monitoring. But the same record also shows the affected grant compliance review segment misses target by 1.3 percentage points, is named in two agency grant commitments, and remains under open legal review for disclosure. The overbroad claim is not that launch readiness is unsupported; it is that the current record proves clean policy satisfaction for certification without a material-weakness disclosure. The better interpretation is that certification support exists only if treated as caveated and not as proof that the disclosure or risk-acceptance predicate has already been satisfied.
claims_about_business_cost: The admissible record supports continuing with bounded monitoring and documented limitations as a lower-friction treatment than escalation, because the system passed aggregate launch readiness and did not show severity-one rehearsal failures. That does not eliminate the named-segment issue, but it does weigh against treating the entire certification basis as operationally unsound.
claims_about_policy: The policy record cuts against a clean compliance finding. The governing text says a weakness is material when it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending. The release policy further says material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On the current admissible record, aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one incidents support operational readiness, but they do not independently satisfy that separate disclosure, resolution, or approved-risk-acceptance condition.
concessions: No admissible evidence shows the 1.3 percentage-point gap was remediated for the named grant-commitment segment before launch.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance exists.
No admissible evidence shows the limitation was disclosed before launch.
The open legal review means the disclosure question is unresolved on the current record.
The 5% projected first-month traffic note does not negate materiality for a segment named in two agency grant commitments.
